_comment: Ceilings and tolerances for tests/perf/gate.py. A metric fails when it is
over its platform's ceiling, when it is significantly slower than the base
commit at `alpha`, or when it is slower by more than `large_change`.
The ceilings are a backstop for a run with no base to compare with (a
main push, a manual run). CPU time per run varies by up to 2.6x between
GitHub's runner instances, so a CPU ceiling sits at about twice the
slowest measured run (startup / per request: Linux 39 / 3.4 ms, macOS
37 / 5.1 ms, Windows 78 / 11.4 ms). Peak memory is stable across
instances (startup / 40 turns: Linux 22 / 26 MB, macOS 20 / 24 MB,
Windows 16 / 20 MB), so those ceilings sit at 1.5x. Tighter would fail
pull requests on a slow or noisy runner for no reason; the comparison
with the base, measured on the same runner, is what holds a change.
reps: startup runs are cheap and noisy, so there are more of them; the
turn workload is a whole session each but still costs a second, next to
two eight-minute builds. With 20 and 15 samples the U test reaches
alpha=0.01 when about 75% of one set sits above the other, so a 10% shift
against ~1% run-to-run noise is caught with room to spare. warmup runs
are discarded.
tolerance: below this change a metric is never called a regression.
alpha: the one-sided Mann-Whitney U test on the two sample sets.
large_change: fails even without a significant p-value.
device: the same 40-turn workload pinned to `cpus` core against wall-time
and memory ceilings, for a machine with no spare cores and a phone's
memory. It has no base to compare with, since wall time on a shared
runner measures the runner; the ceilings are deliberately loose first-run
values, to be tightened from what the runners report.
binary_mb: the release binary's size, in 10^6 bytes. It is exact, so it
has no tolerance or test: it fails only over its ceiling, and a pull
request that needs more raises the ceiling here, where reviewers see the
growth. First values, about 15-20% above the opt-level "s" builds
(macOS arm64 20.3 MB; v0.1.7 at opt-level 3 was 25.6 / 31.2 / 40.0 MB on
macOS / Linux / Windows, about 21% more), to be tightened from what the
runners report.
tests/perf/stress.py: a long session and a large tree, against the fake
model. Ceilings from what the Linux and macOS runners report (October
2026: 26-44 MB, every step under 0.8 s): about twice for memory and
5-15 times for step times, which vary more on a shared runner. drift:
the last quarter's median gap between model requests may be at most
this times the first quarter's, plus 2 ms.
grep_vs_rg: Grep for paths may take at most this times `rg -l` on the
same tree, plus 0.3 s; a search forced onto one thread is not.
